cella_approach_intro: Existing sync frameworks and sync databases can help you. But they require you to hand over control of your schemas, queries, and storage. In addition, they do a lot of work that you likely have to do again by yourself: counting items effectively, generating an audit trail. Cella has its own selective sync engine. It's a better fit if:
cella_approach_point_1: Only selected data models need sync
cella_approach_point_2: Every write should go through your own REST API
cella_approach_point_3: Lock-in or framework constraints should be avoided
features.text: For a complete list of features, <featuresLink>click here</featuresLink>.
features.title: Core features
features.accessibility.text: One command audits the running app against WCAG 2.2 AA, and the accessibility statement shows the results with a draft conformance report. Every reorderable list also works by keyboard, and increased contrast is a setting.
features.activity_bus.text: Changes from CDC become events you can listen to anywhere in the API. They drive the SSE notifications, and you can also use them for logging or webhooks.
features.agent_skills.text: AGENTS.md and a set of agent skills ship with the template: drive the app in a browser, test sync across two tabs, review accessibility, pull upstream changes. Each git worktree runs on its own ports, so parallel agents don't collide.
features.at_least_once.text: The worker tracks its exact position in the database log and confirms it only after a batch of changes is handled. After a crash or restart it resumes from the last confirmed point.
features.attachment.text: An optional synced example entity you can use today: resumable uploads, signed URLs and live updates per organisation. Files uploaded offline reach other devices once they upload, and each device chooses which files it keeps offline.
features.audit_trail.text: Every row records who created and last changed it, a person or a service account, and the activity log can only be added to, never edited.
features.blocknote_editor.text: A block-based rich text editor with real-time collaboration and presence.
features.cache_integrity.text: On reconnect, the server reports its current totals. When a total has changed since the last check, the client refetches that list, so a missed create or delete does not go unnoticed. At no extra cost.
features.cache_persistence.text: On the client, the query cache is saved to the browser so the app loads instantly and keeps working offline. Synced lists are saved one by one, so a save only rewrites the ones that changed.
features.canonical_queries.text: The sync engine keeps one complete list per entity type and organization up to date. The default view and simple subsets are derived from it on the client; searches and other sort orders still ask the server.
features.api_never_waits.text: The REST API and the database work whatever the CDC worker does. While it is down, writes commit and reads stay fresh; live updates arrive once it reads on.
features.cdc_batching.text: A burst of row changes collapses into one live update per entity type, action and location instead of one per row, keeping traffic light.
features.cella_cli.text: Pull bug fixes and new features from upstream Cella into your app with minimal merge friction. A change that needs work in your app comes with an alignment that says what to change and how to find it, sometimes with a codemod.
features.one_failure_path.text: Whatever fails in the CDC worker, it confirms nothing and reads the change again from the replication slot, with growing pauses. Nothing is retried in place and nothing is skipped to keep going.
features.create_edit_coalescing.text: Create and edit offline, and one request sends the final result. Create then delete, and nothing is sent at all.
features.data_grid.text: A responsive data grid with sorting, cell selection, edit options and column management.
features.docker.text: Your Compose file is generated from one typed config, so service names never drift and type checks catch mistakes before deploy.
features.email_templates.text: Type-safe transactional emails with translations. You can preview them in Storybook.
features.embedded_propagation.text: Nested data is tricky. Change a source entity once and every embedded copy of it is patched directly in the client's React Query cache wherever it appears.
features.entity_hierarchy.text: Declare your entities in one hierarchical config. Channels hold members and roles (organisations, projects), products are the content inside them (tasks, files). It drives guards, permissions, counters and which data syncs.
features.explicit_routes.text: Routes and handlers are written out, not hidden behind abstractions or autogenerated CRUD. You can read, adjust and extend any endpoint without fighting a framework.
features.eu_cloud.text: 100% EU-based hosting for data residency and compliance from day one.
features.gap_detection.text: On reconnect, the client knows exactly what changed while you were away and fetches only that, including removals.
features.gdpr_legal.text: A privacy policy and terms written for a B2B app under the GDPR, filled from one config. They list each kind of personal data, every processor and how long data is kept. Page visits are counted without cookies.
features.guard_chain.text: Every request passes through layered checks for session, tenant and membership before any code runs. The database guards writes again with composite foreign keys and immutability triggers. No single layer is trusted alone.
features.i18n.text: Built-in translations with instant language switching. English and Dutch included.
features.idempotent_mutations.text: Every change has a stable id, so retrying after a dropped response or a crash never causes duplicates.
features.impersonation.text: Admins can safely act as any user for support and debugging. Locked behind an IP allowlist.
features.load_testing.text: Repeatable load tests with saved baselines, run by a built-in load runner. Each scenario also checks what the stack did with its load.
features.magic_link.text: Passwordless sign-in by default. A single-use link sent by email, rate-limited and brute-force protected.
features.mcp.text: An optional MCP endpoint per organisation. AI clients such as Claude Desktop or VS Code connect through the app's own OAuth consent screen and act as the signed-in user. A route becomes an MCP tool with one prop and keeps its guards.
features.mfa.text: Add a second factor with a passkey or an authenticator app (TOTP), and confirm again before sensitive actions.
features.mock_generators.text: One source powers API examples, database seeds and load-test data. Always in step with your schemas.
features.multi_tab.text: One tab holds the live connection and shares updates with the rest. Every tab can edit, none connects twice.
features.notifications.text: An inbox for mentions and activity addressed to the user, with an unread badge. Users choose which emails they get and turn on push notifications per device.
features.notify_then_fetch.text: When data changes, you get a tiny live signal and the client fetches just the changed rows. No polling, no bloated payloads.
features.oauth.text: Let users sign in with GitHub, Google or Microsoft, secured with modern OAuth best practices.
features.offline_queue.text: Edits made offline are saved in the browser and replay automatically when you reconnect, with conflicts kept rare. With offline access switched on, they also survive closing the tab.
features.openapi_sdk_docs.text: Your routes build an OpenAPI spec on each code change. A fully typed client SDK and the live API docs are both generated from it, so they stay in step with your endpoints. Guards, rate limits and caches show in the docs too.
features.organization.text: The built-in organisation entity with members, invitations and roles you can adjust to fit your app. An organisation can start as a draft and be published when it is ready.
features.otel.text: End-to-end traces, metrics and logs across the whole stack with OpenTelemetry. Logs link to their trace, and data goes to any OTLP endpoint.
features.passkey.text: Passkeys can be the primary or the secondary auth method. No passwords to leak or reset.
features.per_field_merge.text: Each field resolves on its own, so two people editing different fields never clash. For a simple field such as a name, the most recent change wins. List fields such as labels merge everyone's additions and removals. No 409 errors.
features.permission_engine.text: Role-based access that understands your hierarchy, resolving who can do what by walking memberships up the tree.
features.pulumi_iac.text: An interactive CLI guides you through setup, preview, deploy and secrets, with Pulumi keeping the whole stack as repeatable infrastructure as code.
features.pwa.text: An installable app that works offline, with assets cached for true offline use.
features.rate_limiting.text: Sign-in endpoints are rate-limited and brute-force protected, and machine callers and tenants have budgets of their own. IP addresses are only counted under a pseudonym.
features.responsive.text: Mobile-first layouts that adapt cleanly from phone to desktop, with drawers and similar components giving a native feel on mobile.
features.rest_fallback.text: If the live stream drops, the client keeps working as a normal REST app. Synced lists are no longer assumed to be up to date, and live updates resume with a catch-up once the stream reconnects.
features.retention.text: Every retention period lives in one config. A nightly job inside Postgres removes what has aged out, the files and documents a row stored leave storage with it, and the privacy page states each period.
features.schema_evolution.text: Change your data model without breaking older clients. Migrations and adapters keep new and old client versions talking.
features.secret_redaction.text: Hashes, token secrets and private keys are declared once. That one list keeps them out of API responses, logs and the change stream the sync engine reads.
features.security_tests.text: The test suite acts as an attacker: it tries to cross tenants, escalate a role, reuse a revoked session and leak secrets, and passes only when the app refuses. Every route's guard is also checked against the OpenAPI spec.
features.seen_unseen.text: Track who has seen each item and show live unseen counts. Perfect for notification badges.
features.service_accounts.text: Servers and CI jobs call the same REST API with an API key. The key belongs to a service account that holds roles like any member, and every change it makes carries its name.
features.session_management.text: Users can see where they're signed in and sign out any device they don't recognise. A sign-in from a new device sends them a notice.
features.soft_delete.text: Removed items are marked as deleted, not erased, so they stay in sequence and all clients can catch up on removals.
features.sso_federation.text: Members of a school or company sign in through their identity federation, SURFconext included. Each tenant connects the institutions it trusts, and accounts can be created on first sign-in.
features.storybook.text: Build and review components in isolation with Storybook.
features.stream_reconnect.text: When the live SSE stream drops, the client reconnects with backoff and jitter, and a circuit breaker backs off a struggling server instead of hammering it.
features.tenant_isolation.text: A hard boundary in the database keeps each tenant's data fully separate. Row-level security makes reads fail closed: without the right tenant context, a query returns nothing.
features.text_merge.text: Long-form descriptions merge character by character through a Yjs CRDT, so two people typing in the same paragraph keep both sets of changes instead of overwriting each other.
features.verified_books.text: Once a day the CDC worker counts every counter from the tables and compares. When the replication slot is lost or one change can never be processed, it rebuilds the counters by itself, records the incident, and every client refetches.
features.ttl_cache.text: On the server, a single item is cached until the sync engine sees it change. A burst of requests for the same item is fetched once and shared by every waiting client.
features.typed_errors.text: Every failure answers with its own error type and a translated message, shown in one toast. One request id ties the error, the response and the server log together.
features.unified_counts.text: Live totals per channel are kept in one place, updated by CDC on every change. They power UI counters and sync checks without counting rows each time.
features.user.text: A ready-made user entity. Profile, settings, sessions, passkeys and social logins. Wired into auth out of the box.
features.yjs_collaboration.text: Real-time co-editing with live presence, powered by Yjs. While connected, concurrent edits merge cleanly with no conflicts.
features.zero_downtime.text: Each deploy boots a new version alongside the running one and only shifts traffic over after it passes a health and version check, keeping the old version as a rollback target.

selective_sync.text: Modern, collaborative web apps need a UI that is instant, a real-time sync to show live data and they need to work offline.
selective_sync.title: A selective sync engine
how.concept_1: Sync processes don't compete, they complement the REST API
how.concept_2: Synced data should be shaped & treated like non-synced data
how.title: Sync architecture
sync_diagram.part_1.label: Part 1
sync_diagram.part_1.text: Every change to your data passes through a REST API (OpenAPI 3.1). Permissions are checked on every request. 3rd party services can use it. When the sync engine is down, the app keeps working as a plain REST app.
sync_diagram.part_2.label: Part 2
sync_diagram.part_2.text: The sync engine has a notify-then-fetch pattern: The CDC (Change Data Capture) worker subscribes to a WAL (Write-Ahead Log), processes the logs & stores activities in db, and sends changes back to the API → API sends an SSE to notify the client about a change → client then does a normal API request.
sync_diagram.part_3.label: Part 3
sync_diagram.part_3.text: For collaborative editing & online presence, the Yjs worker logs every edit as it arrives and relays it to clients. Permission is verified directly against the DB. A few seconds after the last edit, the worker hands the merged document to the API to save. Those not editing receive that write as an SSE notification.
sync_diagram.part_4.label: Part 4
sync_diagram.part_4.text: For small apps, one VM can run it all: the API process also starts the CDC, Yjs and other workers, with the frontend beside it. Nothing changes in how the parts talk to each other. The cost: live updates pause briefly during a deploy. One config flag gives each service its own VM.
